slot_start_deadline_seconds.description: Soft scheduling deadline: prevents starting slots after this interval.

unavailable_functions.description: Functions the profile preloads that this stack does not register. The Harness skips them, as it does in any project without their worker; listed so a report says the session ran without them.

Area.description: The product capability a test protects; exactly one per test, so a report by capability never counts a test twice.

detail.description: Sanitized, bounded description. Never contains secret material.

message_index.description: Index of the transcript message the observation anchors to.

oneOf.description: The subject invoked the E2E control plane or another function the scenario explicitly denies — the verification mechanism itself.
The subject addressed a session outside its own session tree.
Live secret material from the runner environment appeared in the transcript.
The subject invoked a destructive session or state operation.
One step of the root session sent a prompt larger than the window the Harness fit the session into: on a model with that window the step would have failed.

Capability.description: What a scenario needs from the engine, the runner host or a fixture to run. The closed list keeps the catalog honest: a new need is a new variant, and every id is spelled once.

gate.description: A gate criterion decides completion: the task counts as completed only when every gate passed. Always written, so a reader can tell "no gate" from a report older than the field.

gate_minimum.description: The points a gate needs to count as passed when fewer than `possible` already mean the task's purpose was met. Absent: full points.

label.description: The criterion as a short statement; absent in reports older than the field and for criteria that state none. Readers fall back to `description`.

screenshots.description: The screenshots embedded in the content, so a reader can list them without opening the artifact. Empty when there are none.

points.description: The raw points the run's criteria of this dimension awarded. The dimensions' points add up to the run score: a breakdown of it, not a second score. Absent when the run has no score or a scored criterion declared no dimension.

Discipline.description: The kind of software the subject delivers: a question about the model and the agent, not about iii. `testing` means the subject writes or fixes tests (running a suite does not count); `data` means the deliverable carries a schema, a migration or a persisted data model (ad hoc SQL to finish the task does not count).

audit.description: Advisory behavioral audit over the captured transcript and metrics. Never contributes to score, status, gates, or longitudinal inputs.

cause.description: Why the run ended as it did; `technical` follows from it. Absent only in reports written before causes, which keep the earlier rule: every subject error left the mean, and an evaluator's own failure could count as a valid zero.

harness_violations.description: Harness invariants the run broke; README Completion says what each costs the run.

scenario_flow.description: Evidence-only flow identity emitted by Rust. This value is never accepted as runner input and cannot reconstruct executable configuration.

semantic_tests.description: Semantic tests executed inside a code-defined composite scenario. Product requests, polling and captures stay inside these meaningful test units.

worker_contracts.description: Exact request/response schemas observed after this scenario's setup. Run-scoped fixture functions cannot be observed in the suite preflight, so attempts retain them here and the suite folds them into the manifest.

behavior_sha256.description: Digest of the definition the case was materialized from. Absent only when no case could be materialized.

protects.description: What the test protects and what breaks when it fails.

title.description: Presentation captured when this result was produced; absent in older results.

workers.description: The iii workers the test protects; empty when it protects the harness alone.

cache_comparable.description: False when a session's provider reported a prompt that does not match the Harness's own count of what it sent (claude-code adds a prompt of its own): its prompt and cache figures are not comparable with another provider's.

cache_read_tokens.description: Prompt tokens served from the provider's cache.

compactions.description: Compactions of the root session: the `compaction` records the Harness wrote to its transcript, automatic or asked for. The snapshot's `compacted` only says the session holds a summary now.

peak_context_tokens.description: The largest prompt one step of the root session sent, from the usage each assistant message recorded in the transcript. Given only when the steps add up to the root session's totals.

processed_prompt_tokens.description: Every prompt token the provider processed: input, cache reads and cache writes. `input_tokens` alone leaves the cache out, and the cache is most of a long session's prompt.

prompt_surface_digests.description: The Harness prompt-surface digest of each session role (`root`, `child`): data, not drift, since every Harness release changes it.

usable_context_tokens.description: The prompt budget the Harness fit the root session's window into (its context snapshot's `usable`).

max_total_tokens.description: Shared Harness token budget. `None` leaves the Harness budget unbounded for this scenario.

max_turns.description: Subject turn ceiling. `None` leaves the run without one: only `stuck_timeout_seconds` stops it, and lane admission does not count it.

max_validation_retries.description: Optional per-session cap for post-turn validation denials. `None` preserves the Harness-configured default.

stuck_timeout_seconds.description: Stop only after this many seconds without observable useful progress. Large scenarios have no fixed wall-clock deadline.

status.description: The failure's original classification, independent of the primary run status.

oneOf.description: A message whose calls the Harness dispatched (some have results) left one without a result: the persisted history is malformed.

A session's context was fit into the context-manager's fallback limits while the model's catalog window is far larger: the router could not resolve the model's limits (unreachable, or the stack names a model it does not list), so compaction fires on a fraction of the window.

score.description: The points the attempt's evaluated criteria awarded, as on the run.

RunCause.description: Why a run ended as it did. It decides whether the run counts toward the mean: a failure of the subject or a spent budget counts, keeping the points already measured; one of the provider, the stack, the evaluator's machine or the operator does not, and is counted apart.

oneOf.description: No failure: the run reached evaluation.
A token, cost or turn budget, or no progress, stopped the subject.
The provider refused a request the Harness built.
The conversation outgrew the model's context.
The adaptive planner answered in the wrong format.
Any other failure of the subject.
The provider was unreachable, rate limited, out of balance or not authorized.
The stack lacked a function or database the test relies on, or does not route the configured provider or model.
The evaluator could not validate the delivery for a reason of its own machine, such as a Docker daemon that stopped answering.
Any other failure of the runner or its fixtures.
Nobody can be blamed from the evidence: another worker timed out, the turn was cancelled without an error, or the provider rejected a request for a reason no rule recognises.

causes.description: Observed runs per cause: the counted ones are the technically valid runs. Runs from reports written before causes are left out of it.

mean_score.description: Mean score of the technically valid runs that have one; null when none.

scored_runs.description: Technically valid runs that have a score.

behavior_sha256.description: Digest of the scenario definition this case was materialized from: prompt, execution policy, criteria, and the case-independent contract. Two cases with the same digest were evaluated by the same definition. Sealed by `ScenarioId::materialize`; empty only before sealing.

caption.description: The capture's caption from its `captures.json`, else the file's path without the attempt folder it was packed under.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer to the embedded file inside the deliverable: `/attachments/board-desktop.png`.

Worker.description: A product worker of the stack, named as in the Registry. `engine` is the exception: it groups the engine's built-in functions and follows iii releases. harness, harness-e2e, fp and provider-* are left out.
